title: On-Prem & VPC Maintenance + SLA/SLO Communication Playbook (Draft)
content:
PURPOSE:
This working draft collects playbook text, Terraform module notes, and customer communication templates for scheduled maintenance and rolling upgrades of private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Goal: a reusable set of templates and checklists that SRE/solutions can adapt per-customer.

HIGH-LEVEL PRINCIPLES (short):
- Transparency: customers must receive staged notices (30d, 14d, 72h, 24h, 1h) with clear impact.
- Safety-first: automated preflight + backups + canary rollout for upgrades.
- Predictable economics: state expected downtime and SLA crediting model.
- Minimal ops burden: provide Terraform-friendly change bundles and explicit firewall/KMS actions for customers.

SLA / SLO LANGUAGE (draft to send to legal/product for sign-off):
- Service availability SLO: 99.9% monthly for inference API endpoints. Scheduled maintenance windows (announced per agreed notice periods) are excluded from uptime calculations if customer opted into upgrade windows in their contract.
- Latency SLO: p95 inference latency < 250ms for single-request workloads on Dedicated / Private baseline configuration. Degraded mode (fallback variant) will be allowed during rollouts; we will notify.
- Error budget: tracked monthly. If exceed, remediation plan (hotfix or rollback) within 72 hours for critical regressions.
- Credits: consistent with existing hosted offering; template credit phrasing provided in customer contract clause.

MAINTENANCE WINDOW NOTIFICATION TIMELINE (templates below):
- T-30 days: initial advisory — high level what and why, proposed date range, expected impact (minutes of restart, config changes).
- T-14 days: targeted window candidate + checklist of required customer prep (open firewall ports, transient key rotation, consenting to reboots).
- T-72 hours: confirmation + exact start time + optional test window.
- T-24 hours: final reminder + point of contact (on-call, Slack).
- T-1 hour: immediate go/no-go check + link to live runbook and monitoring.

EMAIL / PORTAL NOTIFICATION TEMPLATE (30d advisory):
Subject: Notice: Upcoming Platform Maintenance for your Redwood Private deployment (30d)
Body: Hello {{customer_name}} — We will be performing a platform maintenance and minor runtime upgrade for your private deployment in your VPC. Purpose: security and performance (kernel/runtime patches, wheel-level improvements). Proposed window: {{proposed_date_range}} (UTC). Estimated impact: brief service restarts (expected single-digit minutes per node) and ephemeral redistribution of requests to fallback nodes. Action required: please confirm network access for our upgrade agent (IP range: {{ip_range}}) and ensure KMS policy allows rewrap. Contact: solutions@redwood.ai and on-call (pager). More details: {{runbook_url}}
Notes: include an explicit opt-out path and an acceptance CTA.

SHORT REMINDER (24h) TEMPLATE (SMS / Portal):
Subject: Reminder: maintenance tomorrow {{window_start}}
Body: Quick reminder: maintenance for {{customer}} starts at {{window_start}} UTC. Expected interruption: ~5–15m per node. On-call link: {{slack_link}}. Reply STOP to opt out (manual reschedule may apply).

IN-PROCESS STATUS UPDATE (during window) (Slack/Portal snippet):
- 00:00 Start window — preflight checks passed.
- 00:05 Begin node rolling upgrade (node-01 -> node-03).
- 00:06 Observed #requests/rate, p95 latency change: +8ms (OK).
- 00:12 Node-01 back in service.
- 00:20 Completing final health checks and telemetry reconciliation.
Post-close: Send summary email with metrics and any incident/credit information.

ESCALATION MATRIX (contact order):
1) Solutions engineer assigned: {{se_name}} (email/phone)
2) Private deployments on-call (SRE): pager -> slack #private-oncall
3) Eng manager -> Director of Private Deployments
Track in JIRA ticket ENG-4123 (example).

RUNBOOK: PRE-WINDOW CHECKLIST (to be executed 24–72h before):
- Verify latest terraform state accessible and locked. Run `terraform plan` against the target module and save the plan artifact (artifact id: {{plan_id}}).
- Take full snapshot/backups of model weights + postgres/metadata (S3 v4 signed, or customer-provided backup location).
- Verify gateway/networking: iptables, required ports 443, 50051; ensure routes updated for new subnets if needed.
- KMS/HSM: ensure rewrap key is available and admin consent present for any rotation.
- Observability: confirm metric ingestion and alerting targets enabled for the customer cluster.
- Service accounts: check iam bindings and token lifetimes.
- Dry run: run upgrade on canary test node(s) with production-like traffic (if permitted).

ROLLING UPGRADE PLAN (example):
1) Drain: cordon node, drain workloads, ensure KV cache saved to persistent store if requested.
2) Apply terraform module change (see notes below) on single node in canary set.
3) Run smoke tests: inference p50/p95, integration tests, end-to-end health endpoints.
4) Monitor for 15–30m, then progress second node.
5) After 3 successful nodes, increase rollout parallelism.
6) On error: auto-rollback to previous AMI/container image; restore traffic routing; open incident.

TERRAFORM MODULE NOTES (engineer-facing, concise):
- Module: private-deploy/cluster (v2.4.1) change strategy: prefer additive changes where possible. Avoid replacing underlying disk/hostname resources; prefer in-place container image updates.
- State locking: use remote state with DynamoDB lock or GCS lock; always run apply from CI with approved plan file.
- Breaking change pattern: if module requires resource replacement (diff contains ~replace actions), mark change as "major" and schedule extended window. Communicate replacement impact explicitly.
- Example commands (CI):
  - terraform init -backend-config=${BACKEND}
  - terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars -out=plan.tfplan
  - terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json (attach to runbook)
- Post-change verification: health endpoints /_live and /_ready, sidecar connection counts, KV-cache hit rate, disk usage.

DATA MIGRATION / STATEFUL CONSIDERATIONS:
- If an upgrade requires DB migrations: run schema changes in backward-compatible mode (additive columns, avoid renames). Follow blue/green migration strategy where feasible.
- Where KV cache format changes, include conversion tool and a parallel read path until migration complete.

ROLLBACK PLAN (short):
- If smoke tests fail or p95 latency regression > 20% for > 10 minutes, then trigger rollback for last batch.
- Rollback steps: restore previous container image, re-apply previous terraform state (stored plan), run health checks, and notify customer with incident summary.

POST-MAINTENANCE CUSTOMER SUMMARY TEMPLATE (email):
Subject: Maintenance Complete — Summary and Impact: {{date}}
Body: Maintenance for {{customer}} completed at {{end_time}} UTC. Summary: applied runtime patch v{{version}}, rolling restarts, no data migration required. Observed impact: average p95 latency +5ms during nodes restart; total downtime per node: ~7 minutes. No SLA credits triggered. Links: metrics dashboard {{dash_url}}, incident ticket {{jira}}.

UNRESOLVED / DECISIONS REQUIRED (for product/legal):
- Precise definition of "scheduled maintenance" exclusion for SLA calculations — two wording variants attached; need legal review.
- Template for monetary credits needs finance approval (percentage per downtime minute).
- Opt-out/reschedule policy when customer refuses a proposed window (default: allow one reschedule for free in a 12-month rolling period).

NOTES / LINKS / QUICK REFERENCES:
- Runbook canonical page: {{runbook_url}}
- Terraform module repo: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-private-deploy
- Example incident (for postmortem tone): JIRA: ENG-2021 (internal)

ATTACHMENTS (to include in customer portal where appropriate):
- Short FAQ: "Will my keys be rewrapped?" "Will my data leave my VPC?"
- One-page rollback explanation for legal/compliance teams.

END OF DRAFT — ACTIONS:
- Review: product & legal to sign SLA wording (target: 2026-03-17).
- Engineering: validate terraform plan automation and attach example plan outputs to runbook (owner: Priya).
- Solutions: test templates with 2 pilot customers and collect feedback (owner: Miguel).

(Inline comments, shorthand, and TODOs left intentionally — this is a working drive doc; will be cleaned and promoted to Confluence after sign-off.)
